content: The effectiveness of vaginal metronidazole depends on the specific bacteria causing the infection. In some areas, bacteria may have developed resistance to vaginal metronidazole, reducing its effectiveness. This medication may also be prescribed for other conditions as determined by your healthcare provider. Metronidazole is available in other forms, such as topical applications for the skin or oral and injectable formulations. For more information, refer to the respective product details. Mechanism of Action: Vaginal metronidazole works by killing certain types of bacteria through DNA damage. Dosage Forms: Vaginal metronidazole is available under brand names such as Nuvessa and Vandazole, as well as in generic forms. It is supplied as a 0.75% vaginal gel, which is inserted into the vagina. Storage Instructions: Store vaginal metronidazole at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). How to Use: The gel is inserted directly into the vagina as prescribed. Common Side Effects: The most common side effects include: Headache Vaginal itching Stomach pain Nausea Painful or heavy menstrual periods Sore throat Rash Diarrhea Breast pain (specific to Vandazole) Vaginal yeast infections (which may occur during or after treatment) Vaginal metronidazole does not treat yeast infections. If you experience symptoms such as vaginal discharge, itching, or discomfort, contact your healthcare provider, as you may require antifungal treatment. Report any bothersome side effects to your healthcare provider. Serious Side Effects: Although rare, serious side effects may occur, including: 1. Severe Allergic Reactions: Symptoms: Breathing difficulties, wheezing, rapid heartbeat, fever, swollen lymph nodes, facial swelling, throat tightness, hives, nausea, vomiting, dizziness, stomach cramps, or joint pain. Action: Stop using the medication and seek immediate medical attention. 2. Nervous System Problems: Symptoms: Seizures, numbness, tingling, or pain in the hands or feet (peripheral neuropathy), confusion, or behavioral changes. Action: Discontinue use and contact your healthcare provider. Precautions: Who Should Not Use Vaginal Metronidazole: Individuals allergic to metronidazole, Nuvessa, Vandazole, parabens, nitroimidazole derivatives, or any ingredients in the product. Consult your pharmacist for a complete list of ingredients. Drug Interactions: Avoid using vaginal metronidazole with certain medications. Inform your healthcare provider about all prescription, over-the-counter (OTC) medications, vitamins, minerals, herbal products, and supplements you are taking. Specific interactions include: Warfarin (Coumadin): Used to treat blood clots. Disulfiram (Antabuse): Used for alcoholism, especially if taken within the past two weeks. Lithium (Eskalith, Lithobid): Used for bipolar disorder. Alcohol: Do not consume alcohol or foods containing propylene glycol while using vaginal metronidazole and for at least one day after stopping Nuvessa or three days after stopping Vandazole. Serious side effects may occur. Pregnancy and Breastfeeding: The effects of vaginal metronidazole on pregnancy and unborn babies are not fully known. Inform your healthcare provider if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. Vaginal metronidazole passes into breast milk. If breastfeeding, consult your healthcare provider. You may need to pump and discard breast milk while using the medication and for two days after completing treatment. Overdose: If you or someone else uses too much vaginal metronidazole, seek immediate medical attention, call 911, or contact a Poison Control Center at 800-222-1222. Missed Dose: If you miss a dose, use it as soon as you remember. If it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not double doses. Complete the full prescribed course, even if symptoms improve, to reduce the risk of antibiotic resistance. Uses: Vaginal metronidazole is an antibiotic commonly used to treat bacterial vaginosis caused by specific bacteria. However, its effectiveness may vary depending on the bacteria causing the infection, as some may have developed resistance. It may also be prescribed for other conditions as determined by your healthcare provider. Important Notes: Use vaginal metronidazole only as prescribed by your healthcare provider. Do not share this medication with others, even if they have the same condition. Keep it out of reach of children. Avoid sexual activity and the use of vaginal products (e.g., tampons, douches) while using this medication. If the medication comes into contact with your eyes, rinse with cool water and contact your healthcare provider.
